source.title: Disentangling Trainability and Generalization in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Lechao Xiao; Jeffrey Pennington; S. Schoenholz

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally studies trainability across depth and initialization conditions, but uses NTK conditioning and training accuracy in wide-network settings rather than the versions’ CIFAR memorization, shortcut, or initialization comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper's CIFAR-10 training-accuracy experiment bears on V1. Kernel conditioning results and cited results about other work are not separate rows for the claim versions. Reported learning-rate, generalization, and CNN pooling comparisons do not test the listed versions' specific claims.
record.test_reason: The study measures CNN training accuracy on CIFAR-10 and varies initialization variance and depth to test trainability. These results bear on V1 and the initialization-dependent trainable-depth component of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that NTK spectral quantities distinguish trainability from generalization: deep chaotic-phase networks can memorize while failing to generalize, whereas ordered-phase trainability deteriorates with depth. Their conclusions apply within the wide-network NTK regime.
record.recipe_differences: Studies very wide networks through NTK analysis and finite-width CNN-F training on a CIFAR-10 subset; it does not reproduce the cited benchmark memorization studies' model-size and label-corruption recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight variance and depth determine the reported phase-dependent trainability; the experiment also fixes training to SGD, batch size 256 and learning rate 0.1ηtheory.

fits_no_version.finding: The maximum-learning-rate experiment reports failed training when the learning-rate multiplier exceeds 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial NTK eigenvalues predict a feasible learning-rate range in the tested finite-width networks. The experiment does not establish V5's recovery or curvature dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Continuum residual ReLU networks and plain ReLU networks have the same limiting NTK condition number, despite different gradient scaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connections can change gradient magnitude without changing asymptotic NTK conditioning in this theoretical setting; this is not V3's training-error comparison.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2020; the text also lists Proceedings of the 37th ICML, PMLR 119, 2020).
record.problems: The training-accuracy result is an aggregate textual statement without per-configuration numbers or uncertainty. The additional 16k-sample FCN figure is not described in text. The authors note that their theory does not directly apply to insufficient width, large learning rates, or changed parameterizations.
record.rows_left_out: No row for reported test accuracy because test accuracy does not measure the training-error behavior named in V1. Theoretical NTK condition-number analyses and results cited from other studies are not independent result rows for these versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, model-size comparisons, early stopping, and regularization comparisons; the CNN experiment uses only 1,000 CIFAR-10 training examples.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons between plain batch-normalized CNNs and identity-shortcut counterparts, longer-training controls, and Fixup.

Direct training-speed measurements across initializations, Gaussian versus orthogonal initialization, and training 10,000-layer plain CNNs. The experiments do not establish that avoiding exploding gradients is necessary for trainability.
Transient loss recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, sustained edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from initially subthreshold learning rates.
Batch-normalization comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

missing.what: Add the ordered-phase CNN-F training-accuracy result and its dependence on depth and initialization variance. Preserve the authors' qualitative description without inventing per-configuration accuracies or claiming failure after arbitrarily long training.
missing.locator: Section 7, Trainability vs Generalization; Figure 2(a) and caption

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. V4 is tested through initialization-dependent trainable depth, even though orthogonal initializations are not compared. R2 cannot support a directional verdict from the supplied figure text. Kernel-conditioning results already declared in rows_left_out are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, explicit model-width comparison, or early-stopping comparison.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum rates and student width relative to teacher.
Plain versus residual shortcut training error on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; Fixup training without normalization.
Direct comparison of activation-matched initializations, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, and trainable depth of 10,000-layer plain CNNs.
Training beyond the stability limit, the catapult phase, sharpness at the stability threshold, and divergence below that threshold.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: CNN-F
rows.operation_detail: Trained across 20 × 20 configurations of weight variance and depth.
rows.value: All configurations deep in the chaotic phase reach perfect training accuracy.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across configurations; the paper does not report individual accuracy values in text.
rows.check: The perfect-training-accuracy statement is correctly restricted to configurations deep in the chaotic phase. This row alone does not compare initialization-dependent speed or trainable depth.

rows.subject: FCN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a larger CIFAR-10 subset over different weight variance and depth configurations.
rows.value: Figure 6 reports training accuracy; no numeric values or textual outcome are given.
rows.note: The text states that the figure reports training accuracy but does not describe the results; precise values are not recoverable from the figure text.
rows.check: The subject is fully connected, so this row does not test V1's convolutional-network claim. The initialization-by-depth sweep bears on V4, but the supplied figure text does not reveal configuration-specific training outcomes.

relationships.condition: Finite-width CNN-F networks deep in the chaotic phase, trained with SGD on 1,000 CIFAR-10 examples
relationships.reason: R1 records perfect training accuracy across these configurations.
relationships.display_finding: Every tested configuration achieved perfect accuracy on the 1,000 training examples.

relationships.condition: CNN-F networks in the ordered phase, especially beyond the initialization-dependent depth scale
relationships.reason: Section 7 and Figure 2 report degraded training accuracy and a region of failed training; this initialization-dependent qualification is missing from R1.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy degraded and training failed beyond an initialization-dependent depth scale.

relationships.condition: Initialization variance and depth sweeps of finite-width CNN-F networks
relationships.reason: The text accompanying Figure 2 ties degraded ordered-phase training to the initialization-dependent depth scale, supporting the trainable-depth component; this comparison is missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Training degradation in the ordered phase followed the depth scale set by initialization.
